changelog:
Documentation and packaging only, answering the scan findings against 1.1.0. No behaviour changed, no feature was added or removed, and the test suite is unchanged at 1371 passing offline.

The design record and implementation plan no longer ship inside the skill. They remain in git history, reachable at tag v1.1.0 and through pull request 24. A scanner reads a shipped document as live guidance, so a historical record of a defect that was found and fixed reads as a current one, and a historical plan's example trigger phrases read as routing instructions.

A real account's identifiers are out of the published tree. The project id, request and deployment ids, invocation id, domains and route names in the example output and in the recorded API row were replaced with fictional values of the same shape. What made those examples worth having is preserved: they are still real captured output, the field names and types and empty strings in the recorded row are still exactly as the API returned them, and each block now says whether it was captured and redacted or is illustrative.

Token setup leads with the route that does not store the secret. The reference form is the primary recommendation in both the README and the setup guide, the inline paste and the plaintext config file are labelled as fallbacks, and each carries its warning immediately beside it: a token pasted on a command line reaches shell history and process listings, and one written into openclaw.json is a secret at rest that backups copy, so it wants restrictive file permissions and the least-privileged read scope Vercel allows.

Three disclosures moved to where a reader cannot miss them. A provider error message is quoted verbatim on purpose and can carry operational context, so it belongs to the person who asked rather than to another service. An application log line can contain that application's own secrets or personal data: this client scrubs the one token it holds and nothing can distinguish anyone else's secret from ordinary text, so quoted log output should be the minimum that answers the question. And the generic metric surface reaches every metric an account-scoped token can see, not only the web vitals, which is a reason to scope the token narrowly.
summary: Reports a Vercel site's errors, traffic and speed: runtime error logs, failing requests, page views, visitors, top pages, referrers, and Core Web Vitals. Trigger on requests like "what errors did my site have in the last 30 minutes", "why am I getting 500s", "show me the logs", "how is my traffic this week", or "which pages are slowest". Read only.
